record.title: The four-colour conjecture for t-perfect graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a $t$-perfect graph, meaning that its stable set polytope is determined by non-negativity, edge, and odd-cycle inequalities. **Four-colour conjecture for $t$-perfect graphs.** Every $t$-perfect graph is $4$-colourable. The fractional chromatic number of every $t$-perfect graph is at most $3$, and examples are known that are not $3$-colourable; whether four colours always suffice remains open.
record.source_name: Elke Fuchs and Laura Gellert, “On t-perfect triangulations of the projective plane”, arXiv:1702.03175 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: The conjecture that $K_6$ is not reducible for the first Symanzik polynomial
record.statement: A graph is **reducible with respect to the first Symanzik polynomial** when it has the corresponding reducibility property for that polynomial. **The $K_6$ irreducibility conjecture.** The graph $K_6$ is not reducible with respect to the first Symanzik polynomial. This is proposed as a starting point for determining the full forbidden minor set for reducibility with respect to the first Symanzik polynomial; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Benjamin Moore, “Rooted Graph Minors and Reducibility of Graph Polynomials”, arXiv:1704.04701 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.04701

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2017).

record.title: The rational Dyck-path derived-equivalence conjecture
record.statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be two co-prime integers. Let $\mathcal{L}_{a,b}$ be the poset of lattice paths in the rectangle $a\times b$, and let $\mathrm{Dyck}_{a,b}$ be the poset of $(a,b)$-rational Dyck paths. **Rational Dyck-path derived-equivalence conjecture.** The poset $A_{a+b}\times\mathrm{Dyck}_{a,b}$ is derived equivalent to the poset $\mathcal{L}_{a,b}$. This conjectural relation is motivated by the equality of cardinalities suggested by the rational Dyck-path enumeration formula, although the two posets are not isomorphic; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Frederic Chapoton, Sefi Ladkani and Baptiste Rognerud, “On derived equivalences for categories of generalized intervals of a finite poset”, arXiv:1801.05154 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05154

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: The bipartite excluded-minor extremal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p\in\{2,3,\ldots,8\}$, and let $G$ be a bipartite graph with $V\geq 2p-5$ vertices. A graph has no $K_p$-minor when $K_p$ cannot be obtained from it by taking a subgraph and contracting edges.

**Bipartite excluded-minor extremal conjecture.** A bipartite graph on $V\geq 2p-5$ vertices with no $K_p$-minor has at most

$$
(p-2)V-(p-2)^2
$$

edges.

This conjecture extends the known extremal bounds for graphs excluding complete-graph minors to bipartite graphs through $p=8$. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Robin Thomas and Youngho Yoo, “The extremal functions for triangle-free graphs with excluded minors”, arXiv:1801.06887 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06887

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Full-dimension Erdős semi-group conjecture
record.statement:
Let $E\subseteq \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ be an **Erdős semi-group (ESG)**, meaning a sub semi-group of $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and suppose that $E$ has full Hausdorff dimension.

**Full-dimension Erdős semi-group conjecture.** If $E$ is an ESG with full Hausdorff dimension, then

$$
E=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}.
$$

The conjecture is presented as one of the paper's main motivations and is stated to imply Szemerédi's theorem on arithmetic progressions. The supplied text does not indicate whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Han Yu, “Erdős Semi-groups, arithmetic progressions and Szemerédi's theorem”, arXiv:1802.04137 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04137

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

record.title: Forbidden-substring conjecture for greedy universal cycles
record.statement: Let $\textbf{T}(n,k)$ denote the set of strings of length $n$ over the alphabet of symbols used in the paper. Let $\gamma\in\textbf{T}(m,k)$ be a string containing a symbol $a\leq k-2$, and let $\textbf{S}\subseteq\textbf{T}(n,k)$, for some $n\geq m$, be the set of strings not containing $\gamma$ as a cyclic substring. **Forbidden-substring conjecture.** The greedy algorithm starting from $k^n$ generates a universal cycle for $\textbf{S}$. This would complete the known partial classification of forbidden substrings for which the greedy algorithm generates a universal cycle; the claim concerns the remaining case in which the forbidden string contains a symbol at most $k-2$.
record.source_name: Joseph DiMuro, “Classifying Rotationally-Closed Languages Having Greedy Universal Cycles”, arXiv:1805.11641 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11641

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: The consecutive-edge-label conjecture for super graceful matchings
record.statement:
Let $nK_2$ be the disjoint union of $n$ edges, and let a **$k$-super graceful labeling** be a bijective labeling of its vertices and edges by a consecutive integer interval beginning at $k$, with each edge label equal to the sum of the labels of its endpoints. **Consecutive-edge-label conjecture.** Every $k$-super graceful $nK_2$ admits a labeling whose edge-label set is

$$
[k,k+n-1].
$$

The claim concerns normalization of super graceful labelings for matchings; the paper gives examples and no proof or resolution of the general assertion.
record.source_name: Gee-Choon Lau, Wai-Chee Shiu, Ho-Kuen Ng, Zhen-Bin Gao and Karl Schaffer, “Further Results On k-Super Graceful Graphs”, arXiv:1807.01188 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.01188

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2018).

record.title: Subset version of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented simple graph. For a nonempty proper subset $S\subset V(D)$, let $N_k^+(S)$ be the set of vertices $u$ such that $\min_{s\in S}d(s,u)=k$, where $d(s,u)$ is directed distance, and define $d_k^+(S)=|N_k^+(S)|$. **Subset version of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture.** Every oriented simple graph $D$ contains a nonempty, proper subset $S$ of its vertices such that

$$
d_1^+(S)\leq d_2^+(S).
$$

This is a new conjecture related to Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture. The paper introduces it as a subset perspective and investigates related bounds for directed graphs, while the conjecture itself remains open.
record.source_name: Tyler Seacrest, “Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture for Subsets of Vertices”, arXiv:1808.06293 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.06293

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

record.title: The Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture for segment colorings
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a set of $m$ segments drawn in the plane. An **EFL coloring** of $M$ with $k$ colors is a function

$$
f:P(M)\rightarrow\{1,\ldots,k\}
$$

such that if two intersection points $p_1,p_2$ belong to the same segment, then $f(p_1)\neq f(p_2)$. **Segment Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture.** The set $M$ has an EFL coloring with $m$ colors.

This is the segment specialization of the geometric Erdős–Faber–Lovász coloring conjecture. The source presents it as a conjecture; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Boris Brimkov, Jesse Geneson, Alathea Jensen, Jordan Miller and Pouria Salehi Nowbandegani, “Intersections, circuits, and colorability of line segments”, arXiv:1808.07176 (2018).
record.references:

record.title: Converse to the ferromagnetic clique-maximizing theorem
record.statement: Let $H\colon\Omega\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be a symmetric measurable weighted graph, or model. Call $H$ **clique-maximizing** if cliques maximize the relevant homomorphism quantity among the graph class under consideration. **Converse clique-maximizing conjecture.** If $H$ is clique-maximizing, then $H$ is ferromagnetic, equivalently positive semidefinite. The paper proves that every ferromagnetic model is clique-maximizing, so this conjecture asks for the converse characterization; the supplied text states that the converse is false.
record.source_name: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney, David Stoner and Yufei Zhao, “A reverse Sidorenko inequality”, arXiv:1809.09462 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09462

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Infinite-antichain conjecture for weakly fractal matroid classes
record.statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a class of matroids. An **antichain** is a collection of matroids in which no member is a minor of another. The class $\mathcal M$ is **weakly fractal** when the sequence measuring the proportion of excluded minors among the class and its excluded minors has an infinite subsequence converging to one. **Infinite-antichain conjecture.** Any weakly fractal class of matroids contains an infinite antichain. The source observes that all known fractal classes contain infinite antichains and presents this as a proposed general pattern. No resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew, Mike Newman and Geoff Whittle, “Fractal classes of matroids”, arXiv:1907.13343 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.13343

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

record.title: The projective-geometry embedding conjecture for clean tangled clutters
record.statement:
Let a clutter $\mathcal{C}$ **embed** $PG(k-2,2)$ when some subset of $\mathcal{C}$ is a duplication of the cuboid of $\operatorname{cocycle}(PG(k-2,2))$. A clutter is **clean tangled** if it is both clean and tangled.

**Projective-geometry embedding conjecture.** Every clean tangled clutter embeds a projective geometry over the two-element field.

This conjecture is connected with dyadic fractional packings of value two in clean tangled clutters. It is known when the setcore of the clutter has a simplicial convex hull, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Ahmad Abdi, Gérard Cornuéjols and Matt Superdock, “Clean tangled clutters, simplices, and projective geometries”, arXiv:1908.10629 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.10629

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2019).

record.title: Density separation conjecture for polynomial Ramsey classes
record.statement:
For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $3$-graphs, define

$$
e(\mathcal{F})=\limsup_{H\in\mathcal{F}}\frac{e(H)}{\binom{v(H)}{3}}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{poly}}$, $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{part\text{-}poly}}$, $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{polyfact}}$, and $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{part\text{-}polyfact}}$ be the graph families defined in the paper. **Density separation conjecture.**

$$
e(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{poly}})<e(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{part\text{-}poly}})\quad\text{and}\quad e(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{polyfact}})<e(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{part\text{-}polyfact}}).
$$

This conjecture predicts that allowing the relevant multipartite constructions strictly enlarges the attainable edge-density limits. The excerpt presents both inequalities as unresolved quantitative questions.
record.source_name: Jacob Fox and Xiaoyu He, “Independent sets in hypergraphs with a forbidden link”, arXiv:1909.05988 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.05988

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).

record.title: Latin Rectangle Conjecture
record.statement:
For $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\alpha\leq\beta$ and $\beta$ even, fix a set $\mathcal U$ of $\beta$ vectors in $\mathbb{C}^{\alpha}$ generically. A Latin Rectangle for $\mathcal U$ is an $\alpha\times\beta$ matrix whose entries are drawn from $\mathcal U$, with no entry occurring more than once in any row or column. For a Latin Rectangle $L$, let $\operatorname{coldet}(L)$ be the product over columns of the determinants formed from the column vectors. **Latin Rectangle Conjecture.** One has

$$
\sum_L \operatorname{coldet}(L)\neq 0,
$$

where the sum ranges over all Latin Rectangles for $\mathcal U$. This conjecture concerns the nonvanishing of an explicit sum of products of determinants for generic vectors; the source gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Markus Bläser, Christian Ikenmeyer, Vladimir Lysikov, Anurag Pandey and Frank-Olaf Schreyer, “Variety Membership Testing, Algebraic Natural Proofs, and Geometric Complexity Theory”, arXiv:1911.02534 (2019).

record.title: The triangle-free Hedetniemi conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be finite undirected simple **triangle-free** graphs, meaning that neither graph contains a copy of $K_3$. Let $G\times H$ denote their tensor product and let $\chi(G)$ denote chromatic number. **Triangle-free Hedetniemi conjecture.** 

$$
\chi(G\times H)=\min\{\chi(G),\chi(H)\}.
$$

This is presented as a weaker version of Hedetniemi's conjecture, motivated by the fact that the known counterexamples contain large cliques. The source does not provide a resolution of this triangle-free case.
record.source_name: Ryoya Fukasaku, Michitaka Furuya and Akihiro Higashitani, “An algebraic reduction of Hedetniemi's conjecture”, arXiv:1911.09799 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09799

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2019).

record.title: Finite-group gain-graphic excluded-minor conjecture
record.statement: Let $H$ be a finite group, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be any minor-closed class of $H$-gain-graphic matroids. A **gain-graphic matroid** is a frame matroid obtained from a graph whose edges are assigned elements of $H$. **Finite-group gain-graphic excluded-minor conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{M}$ has only finitely many excluded minors, and can hence be defined in monadic second-order logic. This is an analogue for gain-graphic matroids of the finite-field finiteness phenomenon for excluded minors and logical definability.
record.source_name: Daryl Funk, Dillon Mayhew and Mike Newman, “Defining bicircular matroids in monadic logic”, arXiv:2005.04526 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1910.04360](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04360).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04526

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: Rainbow Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture for edge-set families
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an undirected graph, and let $F_1,F_2,\ldots,F_n$ be sets of edges in $G$. For a family of edge sets, let $rg(F_1,\ldots,F_n)$ denote the length of its shortest rainbow cycle. **Rainbow Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture.** If each $F_i$ has size at most $k$, then

$$
rg(F_1,F_2,\ldots,F_n)\leq \big\lceil \frac{n}{k}\big\rceil.
$$

This is a rainbow analogue of the Caccetta–Häggkvist conjecture, relating prescribed edge colours to short rainbow cycles. The paper presents it as a conjecture suggested by the first author; the stated general form remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Maria Chudnovsky, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Non-uniform degrees and rainbow versions of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture”, arXiv:2110.11183 (2022).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.11183

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

record.title: Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,n\}$, let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ denote the family of $k$-subsets of $[n]$, and let a $d$-simplex be a collection of $d+1$ members of $\binom{[n]}{k}$ whose total intersection is empty but every $d$-member subcollection has nonempty intersection. A star is the family of all $k$-subsets containing a fixed element. **Erdős–Chvátal simplex conjecture.** If $k\geq d+1\geq3$, $n\geq\frac{k(d+1)}{d}$, and $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[n]}{k}$ contains no $d$-simplex, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq\binom{n-1}{k-1}=\binom{n}{k}-\binom{n-1}{k},
$$

with equality only if $\mathcal{F}$ is a star. This generalizes Erdős's triangle conjecture; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Jiuqiang Liu, Guihai Yu, Lihua Feng and Yongtao Li, “L-intersecting or Configuration Forbidden Families on Set Systems and Vector Spaces over Finite Fields”, arXiv:2403.04289 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1804.01026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04289

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Characterization conjecture for magic rectangle sets with exceptional dimensions
record.statement: A $\Gamma$-magic rectangle set $\operatorname{MRS}_{\Gamma}(a,b;c)$ on an Abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $abc$ is a collection of $c$ arrays of size $a\times b$, whose entries are the elements of $\Gamma$, each appearing once, with constant row sums and constant column sums in every array. Let $a,b>1$. **Magic rectangle set characterization conjecture.** A $\Gamma$-magic rectangle set $\operatorname{MRS}_{\Gamma}(a,b;c)$ exists if and only if $a$ and $b$ are both even or $\Gamma\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\{a,b\}\ne\{2k+1,2\}$. A complete characterization is known outside the exceptional family $\{a,b\}=\{2k+1,2^{\alpha}\}$, while the cases with $\alpha>1$ remain unresolved in general; the stated criterion is intended to address the exceptional dimensions with one dimension equal to $2$.
record.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, “Partition of Abelian groups into zero-sum sets by complete mappings and its application to the existence of a magic rectangle set”, arXiv:2408.07411 (2024).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1804.00321](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00321).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.07411

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

record.title: Extension of the main theorem without condition (nu)
record.statement:
The Bachet's game with lottery moves model is governed by the assumptions preceding the main theorem, including condition 
$$
, which ensures that each move size from $1$ through $m$ can occur with positive probability. **Conjecture.** The main theorem remains true even when condition
$$
 is violated. The condition is used technically in the proof, but the authors believe it is not essential to the theorem's conclusion.
